clue.text: Put off game — about time

indicators.note: about means going round, so the word for game is placed around the letter for time

parts.note: deer are game animals, hunted for sport and food

explanation.surface: A sports fixture is postponed because the clock is running out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts T inside DEER, giving DE-T-ER. 'Game' looks like a sporting contest but means hunted animals.
explanation.definitionFit: To deter someone is to discourage them, a synonym of putting them off.

clue.text: By working hard, vice-head performed well

indicators.note: working hard suggests the letters are being worked over and reshaped into a new order

explanation.surface: A deputy head teacher who put in long hours got good results.
explanation.walkthrough: 'By working hard' tells you to rearrange the letters of VICE-HEAD; the hyphen is ignored.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who achieved something succeeded at it, so they did well.

clue.text: Climb down, as a sailor must do, we're told

indicators.note: we're told signals that the words are to be heard spoken rather than read as written

parts.note: AB (able seaman) is a sailor, and what a sailor must do is sail, so together AB SAIL

explanation.surface: Descending a rope is something every sailor has to manage, or so people say.
explanation.walkthrough: AB SAIL, spoken, sounds like the climbing term for a descent on a rope.
explanation.definitionFit: To abseil is to descend a rock face or wall on a rope, which is a way of climbing down.

clue.text: A dale in Sherwood forest?

parts.note: read as the end of a name: one of Robin Hood's Merry Men in Sherwood Forest was a minstrel called '... a Dale', and the first part of his name is wanted

explanation.surface: A question about whether there is a valley in Sherwood Forest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A dale' looks like a valley, but it is the tail of a Robin Hood character's name; Sherwood Forest in Nottinghamshire is where Robin Hood's band lived.
explanation.definitionFit: The minstrel among Robin Hood's outlaws carries this first name before 'a Dale' in the ballads.

clue.text: More advantageous for the punter

definitions.meaning: more advantageous means preferable, of greater benefit
a punter is a gambler, one who places a bet

explanation.definitionFit: Preferable is a synonym for the comparative of good, and a gambler can be called one who bets.

clue.text: One snack, or else seven

indicators.note: or offers an alternative, so the words after it are offered again in another arrangement of their letters

explanation.surface: A choice between a single snack or seven of something else.
explanation.walkthrough: 'or' is an unusual signal: the letters of ELSE SEVEN are offered in an alternative order. 'Seven' tempts as a number to count with, but it is only letters.
explanation.definitionFit: In Britain, a mid-morning snack with tea or coffee, taken around eleven o'clock, goes by this name.

clue.text: Bouncer needed at seaside dance

parts.note: the seaside is the beach
a ball is a formal dance

explanation.surface: Security staff are required at a dance being held by the sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bouncer' suggests a nightclub doorman, which fits the dance, but it is something that bounces.
explanation.definitionFit: An inflatable ball played with on the sand is something that bounces, hence a bouncer.

clue.text: A beauty enjoying resounding success?

parts.note: a beautiful woman who is the toast of the party, with 'resounding' hinting at a word that sounds like something rung in a tower

explanation.surface: A lovely woman is having a triumph that everyone hears about.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer sounds like 'bell', which is what 'resounding' teases; the phrase 'of the ball' describes the most admired woman at a dance.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means an attractive woman, especially the most admired one at a social occasion.

clue.text: Terrified by a ghost? Not exactly!

indicators.note: not exactly means the phrase a ghost is to be taken almost but not quite, with one letter changed

explanation.surface: Someone frightened by an apparition, then a coy hedge that it wasn't really one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not exactly' changes the O of A GHOST to A. 'by' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who is horrified or struck with fear is described with this word.

clue.text: Resolve of old Spanish leader to cross river

indicators.note: to cross means to lie across, so the leader's name sits inside the river's name

parts.note: the Dee is a river in Scotland and another between England and Wales
El Cid was the 11th-century Castilian military leader

explanation.surface: A medieval Spanish commander makes up his mind to ford a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to cross' puts CID inside DEE, giving DE-CID-E. 'Resolve' looks like a noun, but it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To resolve to do something is to make up one's mind, a synonym.

clue.text: A shady image is certainly not positive!

definitions.meaning: a photographic film image in which light and dark are inverted
the opposite of positive, saying no

explanation.definitionFit: A film image with tones reversed is a photographic term, and a reply meaning no is the opposite of a yes.

clue.text: Love that's rejected one day in 1945, may still develop

indicators.note: rejected means thrown back, so the word love is read backwards

parts.note: VE Day, Victory in Europe Day, was 8 May 1945

explanation.surface: A love spurned on one day of the 1945 celebrations may yet grow into something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that's rejected' turns LOVE into EVOL; then VE follows.
explanation.definitionFit: To evolve is to change gradually over time, a synonym of developing.

clue.text: Former legislation was precise

parts.note: ex means former, as in ex-wife
an act is a piece of legislation passed by Parliament

explanation.surface: A repealed law used to be very precisely worded.
explanation.definitionFit: Something correct in every detail is precise, a synonym.

clue.text: Heartlessly arrogant and rascally

indicators.note: heartlessly means without its heart, so the two middle letters of arrogant are removed

explanation.surface: Someone is cruelly proud and mischievous.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heartlessly' removes OG, the middle two letters of ARROGANT.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means utter or downright, and in its older sense knavish or roguish, close to rascally.

clue.text: Appeased medical officer's student I found in ploughed field

parts.note: MO stands for medical officer
L, for learner, is a student driver's plate

indicators.note: found in means set inside, so the I goes into the reworked letters
ploughing turns over a field, so its letters are churned into a new order

explanation.surface: A doctor's trainee was calmed after being discovered in a farm field.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ploughed' rearranges FIELD into LIFED, and 'found in' puts I inside to make LIFIED.
explanation.definitionFit: To mollify someone is to soothe their anger, a synonym of appeasing them.

clue.text: Fine wood in Sussex

definitions.meaning: fine means satisfactory, of acceptable quality
a fill-in: this word followed by 'wood' names the Sussex estate near Chichester famous for horse racing and motor sport

explanation.definitionFit: Satisfactory is a synonym for fine, and the Sussex racecourse is its first half plus 'wood'.

clue.text: The result of boat-builder's skill

definitions.meaning: what a boatbuilder produces is a vessel

explanation.definitionFit: A vessel or boat is one sense of the word, and dexterity or artistry is the other.

clue.text: A policeman's on his mettle, you might say

definitions.meaning: a police officer, in British slang
mettle said aloud sounds like metal, and this is a reddish-brown metal

explanation.definitionFit: British slang for a police officer is also the name of a reddish metal, and metal is pronounced like mettle.

clue.text: Do they walk in a measured way?

definitions.text: Do they walk in a measured way?

parts.words: Do they walk in a measured way
parts.note: the body parts that do the walking are also imperial units of length, so they literally measure

explanation.surface: A question about whether some people stroll with careful, even steps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Measured' suggests steady pacing, but the answer is the twelve-inch unit of length as well as the things walked on.
explanation.definitionFit: These parts of the legs carry walkers, and in the plural they are units of length of twelve inches.

clue.text: Thrills, whenever father is with his children

parts.note: Fr is the abbreviation for Father, a priest
a man's children may be his sons

explanation.surface: It is a delight every time Dad spends time with his kids.
explanation.walkthrough: 'father' is not the family dad of the surface but Fr, the title of a priest.
explanation.definitionFit: Shivers of excitement are thrills, a synonym of the plural.

clue.text: It's a mistake not to keep petticoat down!

definitions.text: It's a mistake not to keep petticoat down!

parts.words: It's a mistake not to keep petticoat down
parts.note: an underskirt rising instead of staying lowered describes the phrase literally, and the phrase also means an error

explanation.surface: Warning that letting an underskirt ride up is a fashion error.
explanation.walkthrough: A slip is a petticoat, and one that is not kept down is up, which is also the phrase for a blunder.
explanation.definitionFit: A careless error or blunder is a mistake, a synonym.

clue.text: A European has it in him to be courteous

indicators.note: has means holds within, so the European person contains the other word

parts.note: a Pole is a person from Poland, a European country

explanation.surface: A man from Europe is capable of being well mannered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has it in him' says the word for a European contains IT: POL-IT-E.
explanation.definitionFit: Polite behaviour is mannerly and considerate, a synonym of courteous.

clue.text: Cat gets bird — a blue one

parts.note: a tom is a male cat
a tit is a small songbird

explanation.surface: A cat catches a small blue bird.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition leans back on 'bird': a blue one is a blue tit, for which this is a familiar name.
explanation.definitionFit: This name is commonly given to the blue tit or another small tit, so a small blue songbird.

clue.text: In the distance, a cleric can be seen at the centre

indicators.note: in means inside, so the cleric sits within the distance

parts.note: a mile is a distance
DD, Doctor of Divinity, is a cleric's degree

explanation.surface: A priest can be spotted far off, standing in the middle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' puts DD inside MILE: MI-DD-LE. 'In the distance' looks like a phrase meaning far off.
explanation.definitionFit: The middle of something is its central point, a synonym of centre.

clue.text: Miserable house at Sussex resort — left straight away

parts.note: Hove is a seaside town in Sussex, next to Brighton

explanation.surface: Wretched accommodation at a south-coast resort prompted an immediate departure.
explanation.walkthrough: HOVE is a seaside town beside Brighton on England's south coast. 'left straight away' looks like leaving at once, but L just follows HOVE.
explanation.definitionFit: A hovel is a squalid, run-down dwelling, a wretched home.

clue.text: A fellow may be well-spoken — and well-off

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for fellow, as in FRS
fluent means speaking easily and articulately

explanation.surface: A man who speaks nicely is likely rich too.
explanation.walkthrough: F for Fellow is used in titles such as FRS, Fellow of the Royal Society.
explanation.definitionFit: Being wealthy or prosperous means being well-off, a synonym.

clue.text: Type of hart, or Himalayan goat

indicators.note: type of suggests a variant form, so the letters of hart are set in another order

explanation.surface: A naturalist asks whether this is a breed of deer or a mountain goat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Type of' rearranges HART. 'Hart' tempts as the deer in the definition, but it is only fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: This wild goat lives in the Himalayas, a species with a shaggy coat.

clue.text: In the warehouse, the first supervisor is a tyrant!

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so the letter goes inside the storehouse

parts.note: a depot is a warehouse or storage building

indicators.note: the first means only the opening letter of supervisor is used

explanation.surface: At the warehouse, the head supervisor rules like a dictator.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' puts S, from 'the first supervisor', inside DEPOT: DE-S-POT.
explanation.definitionFit: An absolute ruler who exercises power cruelly is a tyrant, a synonym.

clue.text: Little Derek shows character by joining the territorials

parts.note: Del is a short form of the name Derek
TA is the Territorial Army, the British army reserve

explanation.surface: A man called Derek displays personality by enlisting in the reserves.
explanation.walkthrough: The TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer army reserve. 'character' means a letter, not personality.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the fourth letter of the Greek alphabet, and a letter is a written character.

clue.text: Pan has leg to remodel — and parts of fingers

indicators.note: remodel means reshape, so the letters of pan has leg are formed anew

explanation.surface: The god Pan's limb needs reshaping, along with his fingers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to remodel' rearranges the nine letters of PAN HAS LEG.
explanation.definitionFit: The small bones of the fingers and toes go by this anatomical name.
